the `SecretStore` reads Key Vault **at runtime**, so the next test/run picks it up
immediately (verified 2026-07-25). That is the opposite of secret-injected **env vars**,

**own** `conn-<name>` Key Vault secret, so *one credential shared by N connections exists as N
independent copies*. Renewing the PAT in Snowflake — or writing it under one connection —
leaves the others dead, and **nothing in the product shows the divergence** (#954: datasource
connections have no health signal; #839 gave one only to *orchestration* connections). These

secret they read. **On any credential rotation, write ALL `conn-*` secrets that share it, then
prove it with `POST /connections/{id}/test` per connection** — the connections list will look
identical whether they are alive or dead.

the `SecretStore` reads Key Vault **at runtime**, so the next test/run picks it up
immediately (verified 2026-07-25). That is the opposite of secret-injected **env vars**,
which are a start-time snapshot and do require restarting every dependent revision — see
[[dev-aca-secret-restart-after-pg-recreate]]. Don't generalize one to the other.

unexpected_percent correctness (checked against independently-computed ground truth), and
sample-failure extraction. Also proves the compound_columns_to_be_unique uppercase-column
reflection-casing fix is load-bearing (raw GX call without the fold KeyErrors; our runner,
which folds, succeeds).
"""

import os
import sys

sys.path.insert(0, "/Users/arijit/Coding/Python/DataQ")
os.environ["UC_SQL_PUSHDOWN"] = "true"

from backend.app.datasources.base import CheckSpec
from backend.app.datasources.unity_catalog import UnityCatalogConfig, UnityCatalogCheckRunner

token = os.environ["DBX_TOKEN"]
config = UnityCatalogConfig.model_validate(
    {
        "warehouse_id": "b6403b6e3734f0ce",
        "workspace_url": "https://dbc-4492dde4-090c.cloud.databricks.com",
    }
)
runner = UnityCatalogCheckRunner(config=config, token=token, catalog="dataq_retail")


def show(label, outcome):
    print(f"\n=== {label} === success={outcome.success}")
    for c in outcome.checks:
        print(
            f"  {c.expectation_type}: success={c.success} errored={c.errored} "
            f"observed={c.observed_value} sample_failures={c.sample_failures}"
        )


# ── Group A: reference.locations (8 rows) ──
show(
    "locations",
    runner.run_checks(
        table="locations",
        schema="reference",
        checks=[
            CheckSpec(
                "expect_column_pair_values_a_to_be_greater_than_b",
                {"column_A": "close_hour", "column_B": "open_hour"},
            ),
            CheckSpec(
                "expect_multicolumn_sum_to_equal",
                {"column_list": ["open_hour", "close_hour"], "sum_total": 30},
            ),
            CheckSpec(
                "expect_select_column_values_to_be_unique_within_record",
                {"column_list": ["open_hour", "close_hour"]},
            ),
        ],
    ),
)

        checks=[

real dataq_retail tables. Proves: routing (SQL_PUSHDOWN_EXPECTATION_TYPES), payload shape,
unexpected_percent correctness (checked against independently-computed ground truth), and
sample-failure extraction. Also proves the compound_columns_to_be_unique uppercase-column
reflection-casing fix is load-bearing (raw GX call without the fold KeyErrors; our runner,
which folds, succeeds).

    UnityCatalogCheckRunner,
    UnityCatalogConfig,
)

token = os.environ["DBX_TOKEN"]

    {
        "warehouse_id": "b6403b6e3734f0ce",
        "workspace_url": "https://dbc-4492dde4-090c.cloud.databricks.com",
    }
)
runner = UnityCatalogCheckRunner(config=config, token=token, catalog="dataq_retail")


def show(label, outcome):
    print(f"\n=== {label} === success={outcome.success}")
    for c in outcome.checks:
        print(
            f"  {c.expectation_type}: success={c.success} errored={c.errored} "
            f"observed={c.observed_value} sample_failures={c.sample_failures}"

)

    print(f"\n=== {label} === success={outcome.success}")

            f"  {c.expectation_type}: success={c.success} errored={c.errored} "

## 2026-08-28/29 — #1624 UC pushdown live verification: Databricks Free Edition workspace was inactivity-deactivated
- The `dataq_retail` warehouse (`b6403b6e3734f0ce`) start call 400'd with `resource-gatekeeper` / `denyReason: INACTIVE` — the Free Edition workspace itself had been auto-deactivated for inactivity. The PAT still authenticated fine (200 on warehouse-info); this is a workspace-level state, not a credential or warehouse-cold-start issue, and **no API/CLI clears it** — only a human browser login to the workspace does. User logged in; warehouse then started normally via `POST /api/2.0/sql/warehouses/{id}/start`.
- With the warehouse up, live-verified all 14 #1624 pushdown types via the real `UnityCatalogCheckRunner.run_checks` against `dataq_retail.reference.{locations,channels,categories,date_dim}` — every `unexpected_percent` matched an independently-computed ground-truth SQL query (e.g. `date_dim` fiscal_week≠fiscal_quarter: 535/539 = 99.2579%, exact match). Also proved the `expect_compound_columns_to_be_unique` uppercase-column reflection-casing fold is load-bearing on Databricks: an unfolded uppercase `column_list` KeyErrors (`error_message: "'CATEGORY_ID'"`); the runner's fold (mirroring `DatabricksDialect.normalize_name`, same shape as #1616's Snowflake fix) resolves it cleanly.
- Warehouse stopped afterward (`POST .../stop`, 200) to restore the pre-session state; no credential was touched.
- **Lesson for next time:** a Databricks Free Edition workspace can go inactive independently of the Azure harness (`harness_window.sh` doesn't touch it) — if a warehouse `/start` 400s with `DENY_NEW_AND_EXISTING_RESOURCES`/`INACTIVE`, the fix is a browser login, not a retry loop or a warehouse-config check.
